findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment:
REPEAT- There is not a temperature measuring device observed in the following coolers: 

1. The Grab and Go Drink Cooler.
2. The Grab and Go Cooler containing Uncrustables and other food items. 
3. The yogurt cooler in the buffet area. 

Ensure that every cold and hot holding unit has a temperature measuring device located in either the warmest part of a refrigerated unit or in the coolest part of a hot holding unit.
findings.citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.comment: The bulk dispensers of cereal and the clear display case containing breads, muffins, bagels, etc. are both observed to not have proper allergen labeling. The facility has placed the Notice to Consumer Allergen poster in both areas, but this is not sufficient. There needs to be either a placard, labels, a poster, or some other method that clearly indicates the allergens that are in each item for consumers to be able to easily view. Bulk food that is available for consumer self-dispensing needs to have allergen labeling posted for consumers.
findings.citation_text: 3-602.11(C) Food Labels. (C) Bulk FOOD that is available for CONSUMER self-dispensing shall be prominently labeled with the following information in plain view of the CONSUMER: (1) The manufacturer's or processor's label that was provided with the FOOD; or (2) A card, sign, or other method of notification that includes the information specified under Subparagraphs (B)(1), (2), (5) and (6) of this section.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment: Observed a container of scrambled eggs to be cooling in refrigeration without the required time marking. Eggs were at 68F. Mark the time when potentially hazardous food items are removed from heat control and ensure foods are being properly cooled. Handout on proper cooling practices provided. 750-140b Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F. 750-140(b)  Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 140°F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F or below within 4 hours.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: Observed the following containers of cooked, potentially hazardous foods to not be date marked with the date the item was prepared or the date the items shall be discarded: 1 container of baked potatoes, 1 container of cooked chicken, 1 container of cooked penne pasta, 1 container of soup, 1 container of chili, and 1 container of meatballs. Items were discarded to correct the violation. Staff noted she was unaware when these items would have been prepared. 750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the ate or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

Spoons, knives and forks shall be touched only by their handles.     750-860 Cleaned and sanitized utensils an equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.
